h: From the Grid to the Wolves' Den
p: First time on an indoor track? Don't panic. Most people spend their opening few laps working out where the corners go and how hard they can push the throttle, and that's exactly how it should be. Listen properly in the briefing, because the flags matter: they're how the marshals tell you to slow down, let faster drivers through or come back into the pits. Ignore them and you'll find your session cut short.

A few things make the day smoother. Turn up with time to spare before your slot, as late arrivals can miss the briefing and lose their place. Glasses wearers should make sure their specs fit comfortably under a helmet. If you're in a group with mixed abilities, it's worth agreeing beforehand that it's all for a laugh, as the competitive ones can get very serious once the lap times appear. Have a drink of water afterwards, too; karting is far more of a workout than it looks from the side.

Warrington itself has more going on than people give it credit for. Rugby league is a big deal here, and the Warrington Wolves play at the Halliwell Jones Stadium, so the town has a proper buzz on match days. Warrington Museum and Art Gallery on Bold Street is free to visit and has a fascinating mix of natural history, local history and paintings under one roof.

For fresh air, the Sankey Valley Park follows the old Sankey Canal for miles, with easy, flat paths that suit walkers, cyclists and pushchairs. Nature lovers can head to Risley Moss, a peaceful nature reserve near Birchwood with boardwalks and an observation tower. It's a lovely calm contrast to the noise and speed of the track.
